observations.text: Manual splicing found on one pilot ladder instead of mechanical ones.
Yard diagram and procedure for use of lifeboat recovery strops is wrong.
Lights in oxygen acetylene room should be approved ones.
Fire axes for fireman did not have full insulated handles.
Galley exhaust mesh had oil deposits inside.

positives: Loading master's signature and stamp on cargo plan confirmed discussion with terminal.
style: Brought his own additional questions beyond the SIRE questionnaire.
Expects immediate answers to his questions.
A little rigid when listening to explanations.
Went deep into company procedures and compared them with international rules and regulations.
Super active on deck despite being over 60.
Did not take lunch or dinner, only tea and cigarettes 3-4 times.

questions.q: How did you check the insulation between terminal and ship?
What are the wind criteria for stopping cargo and disconnection, and what if company SMS and terminal requirements do not match?
Does your monthly PMS entry say liquid level in the tube checked?
Before starting COW in a tank, at what level do you check the O2?
What additional corrections apply when checking toxic gas in gastec tubes?
What additional corrections apply in the CCR fixed gauges when you do not have UTI, such as density correction for float gauge system?
How do you check tank pressure from PV breaker when tanks are overpressurized and water tube is unreadable?
What are the COP safety trips?
Is there an entry of discussion with loading master of how much the ship can move ahead or fall back during operation?
How to use recovery strops in lifeboat?
Explain hypermist and low expansion procedure.
Show 1 lifebuoy light if working, and explain procedure and precautions when rigging pilot ladder.
How to check if ship has not moved forward or stern while adjusting moorings?
Start emergency generator on spring mode.
Demonstrate use of recovery strops with actual strops kept in fire station.

tips: Carry a personal gas detector everywhere on deck rounds
Ensure pilot ladder uses mechanical splices, not manual splicing
Check galley exhaust mesh for oil deposits regularly
Verify fire axes have fully insulated handles
Ensure oxygen acetylene room lights are approved ones
summary: Inspector Mansoor Zaidi conducted a detailed SIRE inspection, focusing heavily on cargo operations and company procedures. He brought additional questions beyond the standard SIRE questionnaire and expected immediate answers. Several observations were raised, including manual splicing on a pilot ladder, incorrect recovery strop procedure, unapproved lights in oxygen room, fire axes without insulated handles, and oil deposits in galley exhaust. The inspection lasted about 11 hours, with the inspector active on deck despite his age.
